correctness.rationale: For a centrally symmetric planar Q with center (a,b), its vertical slice length function obeys λ(2a−x)=λ(x), so Steiner symmetrization about the x-axis is centrally symmetric about (a,0). If K is symmetric about the same line and K⊂Q, each centered K slice remains contained after recentering Q slices. Area, convexity and containment persist. Alternating two nonparallel axis projections sends center coordinates to their intersection; monotonicity relative to a centered disk gives uniform boundedness; Blaschke selection and area continuity yield a centered limiting competitor with equal area. The minimal centered symmetric envelope is conv(K∪(2o−K)). For even n this equals P_n; for odd n the old and antipodal vertices alternate into a regular 2n-gon. Their area quotient is sin(2π/n)/(2 sin(π/n))=cos(π/n). Independently reconstructed the assigned seven-blob Git tree and matched SHA daadbeec44206cf0724902be8859e2173f9a356b. Executed the exact verify.py blob after verifying its 1,230-byte SHA, obtaining VERIFY_OK through n=101, and independent polygon area checks through n=200. Neither finite test proves the universal statement.
residual_risks: Uses classical area continuity and Blaschke selection without a reproduced proof of those standard theorems.
Numeric and geometric tests confirm bookkeeping only and cannot establish arbitrary-n or arbitrary-body statements.
Correctness is logically distinct from novelty: a correct theorem can be a corollary of existing stronger results.

originality.rationale: A mathematically dominating pre-2026 theorem was missed by the original review. Fáry–Rédei (1950), Satz 4, as stated unambiguously in the materially read 2022 open-access Horváth–Lángi paper, proves convexity of the volume of the convex hull of two convex bodies translated linearly in time. Apply it to the fixed K and moving -K+2c: F(c)=area(conv(K∪(2c-K))) is a convex function of c. For any orthogonal symmetry g of K fixing the axes intersection o, F(gc)=F(c). The composition of two distinct reflection axes is a nonidentity planar rotation R; Jensen averaging over {c,Rc,...,R^(N-1)c} and the convergent Cesàro mean to o gives F(o)≤F(c), proving the entire proposed two-axis centering theorem as an immediate corollary. For regular odd n the antipodal vertices form the regular 2n-gon, so the ratio cos(pi/n) follows by the standard polygon area formula. Even n are already centrally symmetric. Separately, an existing 2026 published regular-Reuleaux Estermann result contains the same general two-axis Steiner centering argument verbatim in its complete proof, although same-day relative chronology is unresolved. Thus the claimed new structural result and numeric corollary are already mathematically covered; a failure to find the exact formula in a table would not restore originality.
residual_risks: The original Fáry–Rédei 1950 sixteen-page full text was inaccessible, so the audit relies on the precise published 2022 quotation of its general convexity theorem.
The separate same-day Reuleaux finding and assessed polygon finding share the 2026-10-11 publication date; no relative within-day priority is asserted.
The exact cosine expression was not located in an independently read historical table, but pre-2026 general convexity and elementary regular polygon area already force it.
The 1928 Estermann bibliographic references in the reviewed package differ from a widely indexed original article title; historical-source identification should be checked before publication.

value.rationale: The Estermann measure and regular polygons are natural mathematical objects, and the formula can be useful as an educational reference. But the claimed structural centering insight is a routine Jensen/dihedral-symmetry consequence of the established 1950 convex-hull-volume convexity theorem, also explicitly reprised in another published Estermann result. Once a centered minimizer is known, the even/odd cosine area quotient is an immediate elementary regular-polygon calculation; it is not a non-implied unknown natural invariant, a new boundary phenomenon, or an independently substantive structural contribution. The submission therefore does not meet the specified research-value bar, independent of the validity of its proof.
residual_risks: An accessible exposition could still be pedagogically valuable, despite failure as an original research contribution.
Historical exact-tabling uncertainty does not restore value because the formula is an immediate corollary of broad prior theory.

limitations: Scientific rejection is due to rigorous domination by the 1950 convex-hull-volume theorem, not a failure of the submitted proof.
Same-day relative chronology of the separate 2026 Estermann Reuleaux finding is not inferred.
Fáry–Rédei full text could not be retrieved, but its precise theorem is documented in a fully examined 2022 primary paper.
